The SJC unanimously sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery's action, holding that Evans had withdrawn from Presbytery's jurisdiction under BCO 38-3a before the divestiture proceedings began, and instructed the Presbytery to record the irregularity, acknowledge his new membership, and remove his name from the roll.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Craig Sheppard complained that Highlands Presbytery erred by conflating judicial and pastoral procedures after finding a strong presumption of guilt, and by failing to institute process within one year as required by BCO 32-20. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that BCO 31-2 mandates process upon finding a strong presumption of guilt, and that Presbytery was debarred from prosecution because the alleged offense occurred in 2017 and timely process was never instituted; three members dissented on the BCO 32-20 issue, arguing it was not a true statute of limitations and that the matter was never a 'case of scandal.'

artifacts.title: Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE Evans under BCO 38-1 without properly securing his approval of the full statement of facts, as the Investigative Committee's report added additional adverse facts he had not seen or approved. The SJC sustained the complaints of Evans and Pitts et al., annulled the deposition, and remanded the matter to AZP for action consistent with BCO 38-1 requirements; a lengthy concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively analyzed BCO 38-1 confession procedures.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Shawn Keating appealed his divestiture without censure by Warrior Presbytery, arguing Presbytery failed to follow BCO 34-10 procedures. The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, finding that Presbytery erred by proceeding to divestiture without first hearing the minister in his own defense, and voided the divestiture while noting Presbytery remained free to proceed again following proper procedures.

artifacts.title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Sherfey's complaint against James River Presbytery was ruled judicially out of order with defects that cannot be cured, because the bases of his complaint had not been adjudicated by JRP as required by BCO 43-2, and because the complaint to the General Assembly was not timely filed within the 30-day period of BCO 43-3. A concurring opinion by RE Duncan and RE Burnett noted that JRP's commission gave de novo review beyond the Record of the Case and should have narrowly adjudicated whether JRP erred in denying the original complaint.

artifacts.title: Chastain v. Heritage
artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.
